query: Why do resolution duration values vary across tickets?

per_column.name: resolution_duration_minutes
per_column.rationale: This is the target variable of the query itself, derivable from opened_at/closed_at. It is grounded (values are plausible durations consistent with timestamps). As the very quantity being explained it is somewhat definitional rather than an explanatory axis, but it anchors the analysis.

per_column.name: priority_level
per_column.rationale: Priority is a classic driver of resolution time, but the original table already contains a 'priority' column, making this largely redundant with an existing field. Values are grounded in the source.

per_column.name: opened_hour_of_day
per_column.rationale: Cleanly extracted from opened_at and gives a genuine new temporal axis to test whether time-of-day affects resolution duration. Row samples confirm correct hour extraction.

per_column.name: opened_during_business_hours
per_column.rationale: A meaningful categorical grouping directly relevant to why durations vary (after-hours tickets may resolve differently). Derivable from opened_at, though somewhat correlated with opened_hour_of_day. Row values (e.g. 8:50 -> No) suggest a narrow business-hours definition but are defensible.

per_column.name: assignee_avg_resolution_minutes
per_column.rationale: Aggregated per-assignee average gives a real explanatory axis (assignee effect on duration). Derived from in-table durations and assignee, so grounded, though it is a computed aggregate rather than a direct row reading.

per_column.name: category_avg_resolution_minutes
per_column.rationale: Per-category average resolution time is a directly relevant explanatory axis for duration variation and is grounded in the category column plus computed durations.

judge.rationale: The added columns collectively provide several genuine explanatory axes (time-of-day, business-hours, assignee and category averages) directly relevant to why resolution durations vary, and all values are soundly derivable from the table's timestamps and categorical fields with no observed hallucinations. Usefulness is dampened by priority_level being largely redundant with the existing 'priority' column and resolution_duration_minutes being the explained quantity itself; the aggregate columns are the strongest contributors.
